title: An elected government returns after the emergency period
detail: Bangladesh re-entered parliamentary politics after the caretaker emergency, but the wider state system remained tense and institutionally unsettled.

title: Mutiny erupts during BDR Week at Pilkhana
detail: During a darbar at the Bangladesh Rifles headquarters, rank-and-file grievances broke into armed revolt against senior officers posted from the army.

title: Headquarters is seized and senior officers are killed
detail: The revolt led to the killing of dozens of people, including many army officers seconded to BDR, while families inside the compound faced extreme danger.

title: Government negotiates surrender instead of storming the compound
detail: The government chose negotiation and public appeals to secure a surrender, seeking to prevent an even deadlier confrontation in a dense urban area.

title: Mass arrests, trials, and force reorganization follow
detail: The aftermath brought large-scale prosecutions, criticism of custodial abuse and trial fairness, and the eventual reorganization of Bangladesh Rifles into Border Guard Bangladesh.
